author: Thoughty2
description:
The French attempt to build the Panama Canal was, to put it bluntly, an epic fail. But the Americans looked at the whole sorry mess and said “hold my beer”. After dropping a cool $40 million, they discovered that the greatest obstacle to one of history’s biggest engineering projects wasn’t rusted machinery or the frankly terrifying Chagres River… It was mosquitoes.

Once screens and sanitation had brought yellow fever under control, they could finally get to work. Their solution to the Chagres River? Dam it, flood a vast chunk of jungle, create an artificial lake 85 feet above sea level, then simply lift ships into it and lower them back down the other side. Simple!

Ten years and three months later, those plucky Yanks had succeeded where the French had failed, shortening the journey from New York to San Francisco by an impressive 7,800 miles. Not bad for a project that started with everyone involved being eaten alive.
title: The $40 Million Mosquito Problem
